name: IoT & Embedded Systems Lab
tagline: Hands-on IoT learning from sensors to cloud
shortDescription: A connected lab for embedded programming, sensing, communication protocols and practical IoT applications.
overview:
This lab gives learners a structured path from microcontroller fundamentals to connected devices. Students work with sensors, actuators, serial buses and network services using repeatable, supervised experiments.

The environment supports classroom demonstrations as well as project work in diploma, undergraduate and industrial upskilling programmes. Equipment can be arranged for individual or team-based learning.
experiments: Control an actuator from a web dashboard
Exchange data over UART and RS485
learningOutcomes: Select suitable sensors and interface protocols
Design a basic connected device architecture

faqs.question: Can the lab support beginner and advanced batches?
faqs.answer: Yes. The equipment mix can be scoped around foundation experiments, advanced protocol work or a progression across both.

faqs.question: Is faculty orientation included?
faqs.answer: Faculty orientation can be included in the proposed setup and scheduled around the institution's academic calendar.

name: STEM & Atal Tinkering Lab
tagline: A creative maker environment for curious problem-solvers
shortDescription: A safe, flexible maker lab for school STEM exploration, electronics, coding, design thinking and student projects.
overview:
This lab is designed to support Atal Tinkering Lab requirements through accessible tools, guided challenges and space for student-led making. It encourages learners to move from observation and ideation to prototyping and explanation.

The setup can support school maker programmes across different age groups, with scaffolded activities for beginners and open-ended challenges for experienced student teams.

setupTiers.title: School Innovation Lab
setupTiers.capacity: Up to  thirty students, 10 team tables

setupTiers.title: Project Maker Studio
setupTiers.capacity: Up to  forty students, 12 team tables

faqs.question: Is this an official ATL approval package?
faqs.answer: No. It is a lab concept designed to support Atal Tinkering Lab requirements; institutions should confirm their own programme and procurement requirements.

faqs.question: Can activities be adapted by grade level?
faqs.answer: Yes. Activities can be sequenced from guided foundation builds to open-ended student challenges.

name: PLC & Industrial Automation Lab
tagline: From ladder logic to practical process control
shortDescription: An applied automation environment for PLC programming, HMI, sensors, pneumatics and process sequencing.
overview:
This lab helps learners understand how industrial control systems are designed, programmed, tested and documented. Trainers expose the relationships between inputs, logic, actuators, operator interfaces and process outcomes.

It is suitable for ITIs, polytechnics, engineering colleges and industry-oriented training programmes where learners need practical commissioning experience.
learningOutcomes: Write and test PLC ladder logic
Map sensors and actuators to a process

faqs.question: Can the setup use the institution's preferred PLC brand?
faqs.answer: The proposed equipment can be discussed around the institution's curriculum, existing installed base and preferred controller family.

faqs.question: Is compressed air required?
faqs.answer: Pneumatic modules require an appropriate compressed-air provision; the final proposal can include the infrastructure requirements.

name: Electrical Machines Lab
tagline: Measure, understand and control electrical machines
shortDescription: A supervised lab for transformer, motor, generator, measurement and electrical safety experiments.
overview:
This lab gives learners a practical setting for studying electrical machines and their operating characteristics. Modular trainers support demonstrations, measurement exercises and structured lab records.

The environment is planned around supervised use, protected connections and clear instrument workflows for undergraduate, diploma and ITI learners.

faqs.question: Is the equipment suitable for supervised student batches?
faqs.answer: Yes. The lab is structured around protected trainers, guided experiments and instructor-supervised operation.

faqs.question: Can existing instruments be included in the design?
faqs.answer: Yes. A site review can map existing equipment and identify additions or replacements needed for the planned curriculum.

name: Electronics & Communication Lab
tagline: Build, measure and interpret real electronic signals
shortDescription: A practical electronics environment for circuit analysis, signal measurement, prototyping and communication fundamentals.
overview:
This lab combines core electronics instruments with organised prototyping space. Learners can move from component-level circuits to waveform measurement, communication interfaces and small embedded assemblies.

The setup supports electronics, communication, instrumentation and embedded curricula across colleges, polytechnics and ITIs.
experiments: Trace a signal through a circuit
learningOutcomes: Relate waveform measurements to circuit behaviour

faqs.question: Can the lab support both analogue and digital electronics?
faqs.answer: Yes. The proposed instrument mix and experiment sequence can cover analogue circuits, digital logic, signals and embedded assemblies.

faqs.question: Can benches be planned for ESD-sensitive work?
faqs.answer: Yes. ESD-aware work surfaces, storage and handling practices can be included in the infrastructure plan.

name: AR/VR Learning Lab
tagline: Make complex technical ideas easier to see and explore
shortDescription: An immersive learning space for visualising engineering systems, processes, safety concepts and technical models.
overview:
This lab uses guided immersive content to help learners inspect systems that are difficult to access or understand through static diagrams alone. Facilitators can combine visual modules with classroom discussion and practical follow-up.

The setup is intended for structured educational use, with clear device handling, session planning and content review processes for institutions and training teams.

items: VR safety and process simulation bundle

experiments: Identify components in an AR overlay
Explain a technical model to peers
learningOutcomes: Connect virtual observations to physical systems
Follow safe and responsible immersive use
Communicate a process or assembly clearly
Reflect on technical decisions and observations

faqs.question: Is the lab intended to replace practical training?
faqs.answer: No. It is designed to complement classroom teaching and practical work by making selected systems and scenarios easier to visualise.

faqs.question: Can content be selected for a specific curriculum?
faqs.answer: Yes. The proposal can prioritise content around the institution's subjects, learner age and facilitation model.
